# Results — Study 304 (Carbon-Credits) on the real KRBN tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Buy-and-hold KRBN (KraneShares
Global Carbon Strategy ETF, the headline carbon-allowance vehicle, **total return**) raced
against (a) cash — the "is the green bet rewarded?" test — and (b) a time-series (absolute)
momentum overlay that holds KRBN only while its trailing return is positive, else sits in
T-bills (BIL). Sharpe races are **excess-of-cash to excess-of-cash**; the Sharpe
difference carries a circular block-bootstrap CI. As-of **2026-06-17**; the headline window
drops the partial June-2026 month (ends **2026-05-29**). Match the fingerprint to confirm
you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Tape | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| KRBN + BIL (total return) | 2020-07-31 → 2026-05-29 | 1,464 | `cfb978f26c25` |

KRBN listed **2020-07-30**, so the joint tape is **~5.8 years** — a short, single-cycle
sample, named honestly. Nothing here can clear a multi-decade bar; that limitation is the
point, not a footnote.

## The headline — buy-and-hold KRBN vs cash

| Metric | Buy-and-hold KRBN |
|---|--:|
| CAGR (total return) | **+16.2%/yr** |
| Annualised volatility | 28.7% |
| Sharpe (excess-of-cash) | 0.57 |
| Max drawdown | −36.4% |
| **Excess-of-cash HAC *t*** | **+1.41** |

- The level looks like a green-bet win: **+16.2%/yr**, a 2.4× over the window. But the
  reward-over-cash is statistically **not distinguishable from zero** — the excess-of-cash
  HAC *t* is **+1.41**, comfortably **below the inference bar (|t| ≥ 2)**.
- The reason is in the calendar-year table: the entire compound came from **one** year.

## It was one year — the calendar-year breakdown

| Year | KRBN total return | T-bills (BIL) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2020 (½) | +20.9% | −0.0% |
| **2021** | **+107.7%** | −0.1% |
| 2022 | −12.8% | +1.4% |
| 2023 | +8.0% | +4.9% |
| 2024 | −13.6% | +5.2% |
| 2025 | +23.1% | +4.1% |
| 2026 (partial) | −5.1% | +1.5% |

The **2021 doubling** (EU allowances ripped on tighter Fit-for-55 targets and a gas-supply
squeeze) is the whole story. Strip it and the remaining four-plus years are a coin-flip
around cash — two down years (−12.8%, −13.6%), modest up years, a −36% drawdown. A
single-cycle, single-explosion tape can't certify a structural premium.

## The timing question — does momentum beat buy-and-hold?

The overlay holds KRBN only while its trailing total return is positive, else parks in
T-bills (signal known at the close of *t*, return earned over *t+1* — one execution lag;
turnover one-way × NAV). It **loses to naive buy-and-hold at every lookback and every cost**:

| Lookback | Cost | Overlay Sharpe | Overlay CAGR | Overlay maxDD | OV − BH Sharpe | 95% CI | P(OV > BH) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 63d | 0 bps | +0.29 | +7.1% | −50.9% | **−0.27** | [−0.79, +0.27] | 0.15 |
| 63d | 5 bps | +0.26 | +6.4% | −52.4% | −0.30 | [−0.82, +0.24] | 0.13 |
| 126d | 0 bps | +0.07 | +2.2% | −51.6% | **−0.50** | [−1.05, +0.02] | 0.03 |
| 126d | 5 bps | +0.03 | +1.4% | −53.5% | −0.53 | [−1.09, −0.02] | 0.02 |
| 252d | 0 bps | −0.33 | −6.2% | −61.4% | **−0.90** | [−1.46, −0.38] | 0.00 |
| 252d | 5 bps | −0.35 | −6.7% | −62.6% | −0.92 | [−1.50, −0.41] | 0.00 |

- Every overlay underperforms buy-and-hold **before a single cent of cost** (it whipsaws
  out of the 2021 melt-up and back into the chop), and the deeper drawdowns make it strictly
  worse on the very risk axis timing is supposed to improve.
- The bootstrap P(overlay beats B&H) is **0.15, 0.03, 0.00** for the 63/126/252-day
  windows — the timing rule is not just unhelpful, it is reliably *harmful* on this tape.
- The 126-day overlay was in the market only **~52%** of days and flipped **93 times** —
  trading a lot to earn less than doing nothing.

## Synthetic positive controls — the engine is a faithful detector

These are a **machinery proof, never market evidence** (a synthetic Sharpe can't back a
Signal stamp). They confirm the harness banks a reward and a timing edge *when one is
planted*, and finds neither when none is:

| Synthetic tape | Result | Reads |
|---|--:|---|
| Drift control (mu = 0.20, mom = 0) | BH excess-of-cash HAC *t* = **+3.16** | engine banks a real reward |
| Timing control (mu = 0.05, mom = 0.40) | OV − BH Sharpe = **+0.58**, P = 0.99 | engine banks real persistence |
| Null (mu = 0, mom = 0) | BH excess *t* ≈ 0; OV − BH Sharpe ≈ 0 (avg over seeds **+0.02**) | no reward, timing is a coin |

(The null's single-seed draw can land either side of zero by chance — averaged over 16
seeds the overlay's edge on a martingale is **+0.02 ± 0.17 Sharpe**, i.e. nothing.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Buy-and-hold KRBN compounded at +16.2%/yr, but the reward-over-cash
  HAC *t* is only **+1.41** — below the bar — and 100%+ of the compound came from a single
  year (2021). The literature says carbon *should* drift up with a shrinking cap; this
  short, one-cycle tape alone can't certify it. Literature-supported, tape-uncertified →
  **WEAK**, not Real.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** As a standalone holding it is a 29%-vol, −36%-drawdown niche
  commodity whose excess-of-cash Sharpe (0.57) is indistinguishable from cash; the obvious
  "ride the trend" overlay makes it strictly *worse* (lower return, deeper drawdown) at
  every setting. There is no risk-adjusted edge to harvest, with or without timing.
- **Does timing beat buy-and-hold? — NOT SUPPORTED.** At 63/126/252-day windows the
  momentum overlay loses to naive buy-and-hold gross, with P(overlay wins) of 0.15 / 0.03 /
  0.00. On this tape, doing nothing beat trying to time it.
